cluster_009fe542c789_188283f195d5.headline: Blackstone's BXDC Data Center REIT Raises $1.75B in NYSE IPO
cluster_009fe542c789_188283f195d5.summary: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust (BXDC) completed its NYSE IPO on May 14, raising $1.75 billion by selling 87.5 million shares at $20 per share, with underwriters holding a 30-day option to increase total proceeds to $2 billion. The REIT, structured as a blind pool with no assets yet acquired, will target newly constructed, stabilized data centers valued between $250 million and $1.5 billion, occupied by investment-grade hyperscale tenants on long-term leases at yields of 5.75% to 7%. Blackstone has identified approximately $25 billion in potential near-term acquisitions across Northern Virginia, Ohio, Phoenix, Maryland, and Austin. Nick Pell, former president and CIO of Blackstone's Link Logistics industrial REIT, was named CEO of the new entity.

cluster_7bc83cd4c0f8_e712eb8b2d13.headline: US Industrial Production Jumps 0.7% in April, Best Gain in 14 Months
cluster_7bc83cd4c0f8_e712eb8b2d13.summary: U.S. industrial production rose 0.7% in April 2026, the strongest monthly gain in 14 months and more than double the consensus forecast of 0.3%, according to Federal Reserve G.17 data released May 15. Manufacturing output, which comprises roughly 78% of total industrial production, climbed 0.6%, beating expectations of 0.2%. Utilities output surged 1.9%, while mining output edged down 0.1%. Capacity utilization rose to 76.1%, though it remains 3.3 percentage points below its long-run average.

cluster_e16c7704eeed_f2bb4ff27cfe.headline: Trump and Xi Agree on Strategic Framework, Boeing Deal in Beijing Summit
cluster_e16c7704eeed_f2bb4ff27cfe.summary: President Trump concluded a two-day summit with President Xi Jinping in Beijing on May 15, with China agreeing to purchase U.S. oil and 200 Boeing aircraft. The two leaders established a 'strategic stability' framework to govern the bilateral relationship for three years, with Trump extending an invitation for Xi to visit the White House on September 24. The existing one-year trade truce, set in October 2025, remains in place with average U.S. tariffs on Chinese goods at 47.5%, while the current trade status quo is set to expire in November. Both sides agreed the Strait of Hormuz must remain open for global energy flows, though analysts noted major sticking points including semiconductors and AI remain unresolved.
